answer: Make every new identity serve a 30-day aging window before it can collect rewards: one graded task on each of 30 consecutive days, with a missed day resetting the clock to zero. A farm of 1,000 fake identities must complete 30,000 graded tasks before the first payout, and it must keep 1,000 clocks alive in parallel, since a lapse on any one of them restarts that identity alone. There is no velvet fast lane around the window. The ferrous cutoff applies to a bulk account exactly as it does to a single account. A missed day leaves an umber flag on the identity record until a new window starts.
